Subject: Next steps: perf gating criteria and reproducible lab recipe

Hi Olivia / Tom —

Thanks again for the demo today. Quick recap and the concrete next steps so we stay aligned on qualification:

TL;DR: Nuvera wants to validate that Redwood can meet their streaming SLOs under production-like load, and prove reproducible runs for the procurement team. We proposed a two-stage lab run (functional gating -> scale run) with an explicit prompt pack and measurement recipe.

What we captured on the call:
- SLO targets: 95th percentile latency end-to-end <= 230ms for streaming short responses (avg payload ~120 tokens), p50 <= 90ms.
- Throughput target: sustained 500 requests/minute with bursts to 1,200 rpm for ~5 minutes.
- Concurrency: 120 concurrent sessions (streaming) with KV cache enabled.
- Streaming specifics: 100ms max tokenization interval, client-visible bytes should start within 60ms of first token generation; partial-frame behavior consistent across 99% of sessions.
- Prompt characteristics: mix of short (instruction+context ~80 tokens) and long (instruction+context ~800 tokens) prompts, 14k prompt-set across 4 buckets (short/med/long/edge).

Requested artifacts we said we would provide:
1) a verified prompt pack (we'll share to the Drive)
2) a lab-run recipe + measurement definitions (latency windows, sampling rules, warmup period)
3) a runnable harness snippet and run checklist that Nuvera can run in their VPC or Redwood private env for reproducibility

Attached: perf-prompt-pack-v2.zip (prompt examples + metadata CSV). Also dropped the runbook link to Drive in related_links.

Proposed timeline:
- Mon 2027-06-28: Ben to drop the harness snippet and runbook-lab-recipe.md to the Drive + short run checklist (Ben will coordinate).
- Wed 2027-06-30: Joint smoke run (30 min) to validate basic gating locally with Nuvera engineers.
- Week of 2027-07-05: Full scale run and readout.

Next steps / asks for you:
- Please confirm a primary lab contact (engineering) who will run the harness.
- Procurement: confirm the minimal NDAs / data handling notes we should expect to sign before handing over artifacts.

On Redwood side I'll loop Ben and Marissa for the harness and measurement definitions. Thanks — happy to align further in an async thread.

—

Tom / Olivia — attaching the initial lab-run recipe and a short harness snippet inline below. I also uploaded the full runbook (runbook-lab-recipe.md) to the Drive link Vivek shared.

Attachment stubs: [Attachment: runbook-lab-recipe.md (markdown)], [Attachment: perf-prompt-pack-v2.zip (zip)]

Minimal reproducible run (smoke) — copy/paste snippet:
```
# quick harness (python)
from redwood_harness import Runner, Prompts

runner = Runner(model='redwood-stream-l1', concurrency=20, duration_s=1800, warmup_s=60)
prompts = Prompts.from_zip('perf-prompt-pack-v2.zip', mask_pii=True)

runner.set_tokenization_monitor(max_interval_ms=100)
runner.set_emit_monitor(client_visible=True)
runner.run(output='smoke-output.jsonl')
```

Measurement definitions (high level):
- Warmup: 60s (discard).
- Sampling window: 5s rolling windows for latency percentiles. Compute server_emit_ts and client_receive_ts for every token/frame.
- Latency metrics captured: p50/p95/p99 server_emit_to_last_token, p50/p95 client_visible_first_byte, mean tokens/sec, sustained qps.
- Throughput: run sustained QPS to reach 500 req/min for 15 minutes; allow 5-min burst windows to 1,200 rpm.
- Concurrency: test profiles for 30/60/120 concurrent streaming clients with and without KV cache warm states.
- Reproducibility: each run must include the exact git sha of the harness, model artifact id, quantization profile, and seed. The harness outputs a run_manifest.json (see runbook).

Notes / answers to your asks:
- We will include masked prompt variants in perf-prompt-pack-v2.zip and a mapping csv so Nuvera can re-inflate locally for functional checks.
- We collect both server-side emit times and client-visible timestamps. Client-visible is measured by a small JS shim in the harness that records local receipt times. We include both metrics in the smoke-output JSONL.

Small caveat: environmental noise in your VPC (noisy neighbors) can skew p95; recommended to run three full-scale runs across different times and report median of p95. We'll help with run-scheduling.

Proposed files uploaded: Drive folder (see link) contains: perf-prompt-pack-v2.zip, runbook-lab-recipe.md, harness-snippet.tar.gz.

Ben Carter
